newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends weak on commercial hedging, options.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends weak on commercial hedging, options.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended mixed on a late sell-off tied to commercial hedging with bearish options trade cited, traders said.
Funds held the market early but buying interest waned, leaving little support under the commercial hedges.
Cargill Inc sold at least four million bushels March on
the day while Farmers Commodities Corp bought and sold one million March, traders said.

The commercial selling suggested that recent gains in corn had attracted some farmer selling. Cash grain dealers had said cold weather and a bullish mindset was capping farmer sales. Commercial hedging appeared in the options pit as well
where volume was said to be very heavy.

In options trade, Louis Dreyfus reportedly bought 2,000 March $2.70 puts at 1-7/8 to two cents per bushel. Farmers Commodities Corp bought 400 March $2.90 puts and sold 400 March $3.00 puts. ADM sold 200 December $2.60 puts and 100
Refco Inc bought 700 March $2.70 calls and sold 700 May $2.80 calls, traders said.
Corn closed 1/2 cent per bushel lower to 3/4 cent higher with March down 1/4 at $2.74-3/4.

Funds were strong buyers early, accounting for at least 15 million bushels. Prudential Securities reportedly bought seven million bushels and E.D. and F. Man International each bought three million bushels March, traders said.

Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 48,000 contracts, above Monday's actual volume of 44,265 contracts. Options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, also above Monday's 14,413 contracts.
